title: Pleasing God · Chapter 3: Alternatives to Pleasing God
speaker: Joshua Heward-Mills
text:
Chapter 3

# Alternatives to Pleasing God

So we make it our goal to please him, whether we are at home in the body or away from it.

2 Corinthians 5:9 (NIV)

Sometimes you locate the right thing by the process of elimination. If seven people are talking and you want to hear what one person is saying, you tell six people to keep quiet so you can hear the seventh. Sometimes, to find out who you are really pleasing, you may have to find out who you should not be pleasing.

Everything you do in life is aiming to please or impress somebody—everything, without exception. Look at the shoes you're wearing. You're wearing those shoes to please somebody, even if it's yourself. You came to church to please somebody. What you don't realise is that everything you're doing is pleasing somebody. So the question is: who am I pleasing?

Before going further, consider five desires or visions you have for your life. What do you want to do, become, buy, or change? Keep those decisions in mind as we examine the alternatives. Who is each decision intended to please?

The believer's constant ambition should be to please God. A career, a country to live in, a marriage, or a ministry cannot take His place as the ultimate aim. Whatever pleasing Him requires, that is what we should want to do.

# 1. Living to please yourself.

We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

Romans 15:1 (KJV)

We've got a choice. Do we want to please ourselves? What you're doing, who is it for? What you're deciding, who is it for?

Christ died for everyone. He died so that those who live should not live for themselves anymore. They should live for Christ. He died for them and was raised again.

2 Corinthians 5:15 (NIrV)

Christ died for all. Those who live are no longer to live for themselves, but for Him. We often speak about His death in relation to forgiveness, but this verse also tells us something about the purpose of the life we now live.

Who is your decision for? Be honest. When a young man describes the exact appearance, height, or background he insists his wife must have, whose desire is governing that list? Is he describing what Christ has asked for, or what he personally wants?

A woman may say that all she wants is somebody who fears God. But when a God-fearing man appears, it becomes clear that there is a much longer list. Examine the list. Is it submitted to God, or has God's name been placed at the top of an arrangement made entirely for yourself?

The same question applies to ministry. A person may want to become a full-time minister because the life appears easier. I once told a pastor who wanted to enter full-time ministry to gather a hundred members and return so we could discuss it. The person remained in church, but that conversation did not return. Looking at ministry from the outside is different from carrying its responsibilities.

Marriage is also more complex than it appears at a wedding. When I attend a wedding, I feel the need to pray for the couple. I do not simply envy the ceremony and wish to repeat the experience. People need God's help for the life ahead of them.

Do not enter ministry because you like the appearance of it. If God has not called you, there are other kinds of work you can do. Preaching is not merely gathering four points, telling a few stories, and standing in front of people. The call of God matters.

And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.

Galatians 5:24 (KJV)

The flesh has its own desires, and those desires are different from the desires God has for you. These two words—affections and lusts—are two things that have to be killed in you. It's not just to say, “I'm subduing the flesh.” No, its affections and its lusts. These are the things that drive us. An affection is what you are fond of.

Even a preacher has to examine this. I could announce a series on a popular subject and know that it would attract attention. But why am I choosing the subject? Is it what God wants, or is it something I enjoy preaching? My own enjoyment cannot become the final test.

So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

Romans 8:8 (KJV)

Those who are in the flesh cannot please God. Therefore it is not enough to say, “This is the right thing for me.” Right according to whom? Pleasing to whom?

Look at Jesus in Gethsemane.

“Father, if you are willing, please take this cup of suffering away from me. Yet I want your will to be done, not mine.”

Luke 22:42 (NLT)

The suffering before Him was real. He did not pretend that the cup was something His humanity naturally desired. Yet He submitted His will to the Father's will. Obedience involved a choice.

For even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell on me.

Romans 15:3 (KJV)

Christ pleased not Himself. We must allow those words to challenge our own decisions. There are times when I feel tired and would prefer not to go and minister. Then I have to decide whether I am following God's direction or simply satisfying myself.

The culture around us repeatedly says, “Do what makes you happy.” Avoid whatever feels unpleasant. Leave whatever costs you joy. But Jesus gave a different invitation.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.

Luke 9:23 (KJV)

In our time they say, “Do you.” No, don't do you. “Do what makes you happy.” Now I'm just going to happy myself. Anything that takes away your joy, anything that makes you sad—go away from it. It's a culture of self-pleasing. But Jesus said, if anyone wants to come after Me, he should deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.

# 2. Living to please men.

For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

Galatians 1:10 (KJV)

“Men” includes all the human beings in your life: parents, spouse, children, employer, friends, and pastor. Any of them can become an alternative to God as the person whose approval governs your conduct.

The biggest deception that makes us please men is a feeling that my life, and how my life will go, depends on how a human being feels or thinks about me. I'll say this is one of the deepest, most difficult deceptions to remove in most Christians I know. It's not true. No human being holds that power over anybody's life.

For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south. But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.

Psalm 75:6-7 (KJV)

God is the judge. He sets one up and puts another down. Human displeasure is not the final authority over a believer's life.

Suppose your employer asks when you arrived at work. Nobody else was there, and you know that a lie could escape detection. If you tell the truth, you may face a serious consequence. Whom will you please? Your employer may prefer the answer that protects your position, but God knows the truth.

It takes faith to choose obedience when you can see an immediate cost. Yet keeping a job through dishonesty can mean losing something greater. Losing a position because you would not lie does not mean that the One who promotes has lost the power to lift you.

Even a pastor's approval can be different from God's approval. A minister may like you, lay hands on you, or appoint you while not knowing the hidden things in your life.

And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.

Hebrews 5:4 (KJV)

Consider Samuel, the prophet through whom kings were appointed. When Israel rejected his leadership and asked for a king, God told Samuel that the people had rejected Him.

And the LORD said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.

1 Samuel 8:7 (KJV)

This was a man with real spiritual authority. Yet when he entered Jesse's house and saw Eliab, he reached a conclusion that God did not share.

And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the LORD’s anointed is before him. But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

1 Samuel 16:6-7 (KJV)

The pastor was sure, but the pastor was wrong. “Surely this is the Lord's anointed.” But God said, “I have refused him.” No matter how gifted and anointed, he's just a man. When he sees, he only sees so far, because he's a man. But God is looking at the heart.

Seven sons passed before Samuel, and none was the one God had chosen. David was not even initially presented. God called for the person whom men had left in the field.

Again, Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, The LORD hath not chosen these. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither. And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he. Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.

1 Samuel 16:10-13 (KJV)

This should direct our attention away from managing impressions and towards the condition of the heart. David did not gain his place by arranging to be the most impressive person in the room. The One who saw him in the field was able to call for him.

People have been appointed to positions in church, but those under them are suffering. They are wicked, unforgiving. Those things in Galatians 5—love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness—they don't have them. She's not gentle at all, but it's almost like God hasn't seen.

But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

Galatians 5:22-23 (KJV)

The people under that leadership also face a test. Another person's fault does not give us permission to lose humility, become bitter, or disobey God. Each person must attend to his own vessel.

That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour;

1 Thessalonians 4:4 (KJV)

Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said, Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

Job 40:1-2 (KJV)

Do not spend all your energy attempting to correct somebody else while ignoring what God is addressing in you. When people praise my preaching, that praise can become a distraction if I forget to ask whether God is pleased with my own life.

Pain is not proof that God has rejected somebody. Scripture even speaks of the suffering of Christ in terms of the Father's purpose.

Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand.

Isaiah 53:10 (KJV)

At the same time, apparent spiritual activity is not proof that everything is well. A husband can pray for a long time while failing to treat his wife according to God's Word.

Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.

1 Peter 3:7 (KJV)

How can I say I'm doing well when everybody is clapping and I know that I don't even spend time with God? How can I say I'm doing well when I go home and treat my wife badly? How can I say I'm doing well when I'm full of bitterness, anger, and unforgiveness? I have so much pride that nobody above me can even call and talk to me. And I'm doing well because you clapped? What about what God thinks?

Daniel faced a clear conflict between a royal decree and prayer to God. He did not abandon prayer to preserve the approval of the authorities.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.

Daniel 6:10 (KJV)

The decree brought him into danger, but God remained able to preserve him and lift him. Human opposition did not cancel God's authority over his future.

So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

Daniel 6:28 (KJV)

Compare that with Er. The decisive description of Er is not what people thought about him, but what he was in God's sight.

And Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him.

Genesis 38:7 (KJV)

Does this mean we should disregard parents, employers, pastors, or other authorities? No. On the contrary, we must obey what God has said about our relationships with them.

Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

Hebrews 13:17 (KJV)

I obey because I want to obey God's Word, not because human approval has replaced His. The outward act may look the same, but the motive matters.

Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men:

1 Thessalonians 2:15 (KJV)

Do not make conflict with the people God has placed over you a casual thing. But neither should a word of approval from them become a reason to stop examining yourself before Him.

For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.

John 12:43 (KJV)

They loved the praise of men more than the praise of God. Which one do you like? A loud handclap, a standing ovation: “What a word!” Or the single, solitary, almost indecipherable, still small voice of approval from the Master. One person. Which one do you want? You get to choose all through your life.

And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

Matthew 3:17 (KJV)

Whose smile are you living for? Whose applause are you trying to obtain? We have to choose.

# 3. Living to please the world.

“If the world hates you [and it does], know that it has hated Me before it hated you. If you belonged to the world, the world would love [you as] its own and would treat you with affection. But you are not of the world [you no longer belong to it], but I have chosen you out of the world. And because of this the world hates you.

John 15:18-19 (AMP)

The world is a set of standards, a general pattern that we exist in here on earth. It's the general opinion, mindset, and way of life that the majority of society prefers and approves of. We're constantly under pressure to gain the approval of this world and live in the way this world views as great.

Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:

Ephesians 2:2 (KJV)

There is a course of this world, a pattern people are expected to follow. You can be trying to satisfy that pattern without any one person having instructed you to do so.

I once spoke with a wife who was dissatisfied with the money her husband provided. As we discussed it, it became clear that the expectations around her had been shaped by friends whose arrangements with older men gave them a particular lifestyle. A worldly standard was being brought into the home as the measure of what her husband should supply.

We must ask where a standard has come from. Is it God's Word, or is it the system we want to fit into?

I remember watching an interview in which Rick Warren was repeatedly pressed about controversial matters. The response that stayed with me was his resolve to fear God's disapproval more than the disapproval of the interviewer or the audience. A minister has to settle that question. Otherwise the possibility of being disliked or excluded will decide what he says.

Churches face this pressure too. We can become eager to look respectable to the educated, fashionable, or influential parts of society. Then things that belong to our Pentecostal and charismatic convictions become embarrassing to us: speaking in tongues, healing, laying hands on people, and the manifestations of the Holy Spirit.

I do not want us to become a church that gives seminars while being ashamed of the Spirit's work. I respect other Christian traditions and the great things they have accomplished. Many have taken the gospel far beyond places we have reached. Respecting them does not require us to abandon what God has given us in order to appear more acceptable to the world.

There is a pressure to hide anything that makes us look unusual. We must decide whether we are trying to please the world or obey God.

But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world.

Galatians 6:14 (KJV)

The cross separates us from the world. It involves accepting rejection, mockery, loneliness, pain, and shame rather than making acceptance our highest purpose.

In an office where I worked, I did not need to announce repeatedly that I was a Christian. My choices made me different. When people ordered drinks, I could ask for water or a soft drink. When an arrangement arose that I could not join, I declined. People soon knew that there were things I would not be part of.

Embrace that oddity. Accept being strange, rejected, unliked, different, weird in the office. That's the cross. I accept the accusations. Laugh at me. Mock me. Make me look funny and silly. I embrace it.

No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.

2 Timothy 2:4 (KJV)

Entanglement makes obedience difficult. We live in the world and know unbelievers, but some relationships become so deep and controlling that we feel unable to say no. Every invitation becomes compulsory. Every group exerts a claim. We cannot fight the fight of faith while giving every worldly attachment the right to direct us.

Think about the cross. Jesus' disciples forsook Him. He suffered pain, exposure, false accusation, and mockery. Are we willing to follow Him when following brings something of that cost?

People who serve God may have stories told about them that they cannot control. If protecting a flawless public image becomes our chief concern, it can prevent us from obeying Him.

I visited Lakewood Church in Houston and saw that even a minister whose message appeared gentle and encouraging could face intense criticism. Avoiding controversy is not a guarantee that everybody will approve of you.

Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.

Matthew 5:11-12 (KJV)

Jesus told us how to respond when we are falsely reviled for His sake. The prophets before us were persecuted too. We cannot join their line while demanding a life in which nobody ever speaks against us.

Even the resurrection was met with a false story about the disciples stealing the body.

And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers, Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept. And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you. So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.

Matthew 28:12-15 (KJV)

The apostles did not make the correction of every accusation their life's work. They went on with what God had called them to do.

Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

Luke 6:26 (KJV)

Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.

2 Timothy 3:12 (KJV)

Do not be so determined to receive universal approval that you cannot bear somebody making a joke or a false accusation about you. A Christian life cannot be measured by whether everybody speaks well of it.

A friend once asked to speak to me merely as the friend he used to know, rather than as a pastor. I explained that the person he was trying to call back was no longer the same. Christ had changed my life.

Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.

2 Corinthians 5:17 (KJV)

I want to be able to share what God is putting on my heart. That belongs to friendship too.

Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.

John 15:15 (KJV)

If the things of God can never enter a friendship, that friendship is placing a serious limit on the person I have become in Christ.

# 4. Living to please Satan.

You belong to your father, the devil. You want to obey your father’s wishes. From the beginning, the devil was a murderer. He has never obeyed the truth. There is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his natural language. He does this because he is a liar. He is the father of lies.

John 8:44 (NIrV)

We often say that God has a plan for our lives. We should also understand that Satan has things he wants us to do. His wishes are not the same as God's wishes.

Satan never announces. He's a trickster. He tricks you into doing what he wants. He doesn't say, “Here's my plan. Follow it.” No, no. You'll be so convinced you're doing the right thing. So convinced you'll even teach others.

Eve described what happened to her.

And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

Genesis 3:13 (KJV)

The serpent beguiled her, and she ate. The decision fulfilled what the serpent wanted.

This is why we must not make happiness our ultimate test. There is a satisfaction in God's will that self-pleasing cannot supply. Consider Jesus at the well in Samaria. He was weary, and the disciples had gone to buy food. His physical need was real. Yet after ministering to the woman, He spoke about another source of nourishment.

Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour. There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink. (For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy meat.)

John 4:6-8 (KJV)

In the mean while his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat. But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not of. Therefore said the disciples one to another, Hath any man brought him ought to eat? Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.

John 4:31-34 (KJV)

The Living Bible calls it “My nourishment”:

Then Jesus explained: “My nourishment comes from doing the will of God who sent me, and from finishing his work.

John 4:34 (TLB)

His meat was to do the will of the One who sent Him and finish His work. There is a satisfaction in obedience that the world does not understand.

But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

Matthew 4:4 (KJV)

Bread is not the whole answer to a man's life. We must live by the Word of God.

During an encounter in which a young person was manifesting an evil spirit, I heard statements about matters in my life that were strikingly accurate. The statements touched real feelings and experiences. But along with those truths came advice that would have led me away from what God wanted.

The Holy Spirit used it to teach me something: Satan is really a trickster. The best way to lie is to add some truth. “Where did you go?” “I went out with Ralph. We went to watch a movie.” It's true. You told your mother the truth. But Ralph and who? After the movie, where did you go? Where did you watch it—a cinema or somebody's bedroom? A lot of details are left out. That's how Satan tricks you.

In the same way, a thought may correctly identify that somebody has treated you badly and then attach a wrong instruction: “Therefore leave the place where God has put you.” The first observation may be true, but the conclusion can still be deception.

We need to lay the axe at the root. How did you come to this place? What was the mistake? Unless the root is addressed, a second chance may simply produce the same choice again.

I have watched people leave a painful relationship and then choose almost the same thing again. Sometimes even the outward resemblance is striking. The person thinks the previous problem was the appearance or personality of the other person. But the deeper problem may have been disobedience, worldliness, or a refusal to listen.

The problem was not the fruit. The root is what made this tree exist. When you're solving a problem, put the axe at the root. The problem is disobedience. It's not that you'll never choose somebody with long hair again because the long hair was the problem. The long hair was never the problem. The problem is that you don't listen.

And the LORD God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:

Genesis 3:14 (KJV)

There are three lies in the temptation in Eden that we must recognise.

# a. “You will not die.”

And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:

Genesis 3:4 (KJV)

We live as though time cannot finish. We imagine that obedience can always be postponed, that there will be another opportunity to put things right, honour somebody, or respond to God.

Even practical responsibilities can reveal this deception. A parent may say that a will has been written without considering whether its arrangements will leave the children fighting over a shared house. One child wants to live there, another wants to keep it as a family home, and another needs it sold. We should think seriously rather than assuming that death belongs to a distant, unreal future.

Your time matters. Do not assume that an opportunity to do what is right will always remain.

# b. “You will be as God.”

For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

Genesis 3:5 (KJV)

This is the thought that nobody should tell you what to do, that your life belongs entirely to you, and that you are the final authority. It makes submission sound like an insult and obedience like an unnecessary loss of control.

But we are not God. We must not take the steering wheel from Him and call our independence spiritual maturity.

# c. “God's Word is not really true.”

Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

Genesis 3:1 (KJV)

“Hath God said?” The question weakens confidence in what God has spoken. We may not deny the Bible openly. We simply treat its warnings as less true, less serious, or less applicable than they are.

Is it really true that to be carnally minded is death? That sowing to the flesh brings corruption? That there is a judgment? That a man's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions?

For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.

Romans 8:6 (KJV)

Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

Galatians 6:7-8 (KJV)

And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats: And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.

Matthew 25:32-33 (KJV)

And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

Matthew 7:23 (KJV)

And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

Luke 12:15 (KJV)

Will we take seriously the spiritual realities Scripture describes and the commands God has given?

Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

Hebrews 11:3 (KJV)

Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

Matthew 22:37-40 (KJV)

I will bring it forth, saith the LORD of hosts, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name: and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof.

Zechariah 5:4 (KJV)

We can call ourselves believers while inwardly reducing what we believe. “It is true, but surely not that true.” That is a dangerous place. The serpent's question still works when it persuades us to doubt the consequence of disobedience.

# Examine your decisions.

Look at your decisions again and assess them. Are you building a house? Why? Are you changing your phone? Why? When you said yes, or you said no—or yes after the no—who were we pleasing? Whose smile are we fighting for? Whose applause are we contending for?

There have been times when I received some money and immediately began thinking about what I would do with it. Then I sensed the Holy Spirit asking whether I would seek His guidance. Even a seemingly ordinary decision can reveal how independently we have learned to think.

Remember Daniel. He prospered during the reign of the very king whose decree had brought him into danger. God's approval was not powerless in the presence of human authority.

I learned deeply, during a season in London in 2015, that pleasing God is better. Human reactions pass. People's anger, opinions, and comments do not last forever. God remains.

When you say yes or no, ask whom that answer is intended to please. Why do you obey a pastor? Because you fear trouble with a person, or because God's Word tells you to submit? Why did you lie? Could a lie possibly be an act intended to make God happy?

Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.

Acts 5:29 (KJV)

The alternatives are to please yourself, men, the world, or Satan. There is another choice: live to please God.
